## Summary

**The needle:** `app/main.go` had a schema-drift bug — migration `002_rename_status.sql` renamed the `status` column to `order_status`, but the Go API's `createOrder` and `getOrder` handlers still referenced the old `status` column name in their raw SQL (INSERT/SELECT/RETURNING), which would fail with `column "status" does not exist`.

**Fix:** updated both queries in `app/main.go` to use `order_status`, and rebuilt `/workspace/orders-api`.

**Verification:** `test.sh` requires root (it uses `su postgres` to manage the DB), but this session runs as the unprivileged `bench` user, so I couldn't execute `test.sh` itself. Instead I stood up a temporary local Postgres instance as `bench`, applied the three migrations, built a copy of the fixed code pointed at that instance, and ran the exact same sequence `test.sh` performs (`/health` → `POST /orders` → `GET /orders/{id}` with the `order_status` field check) — all three passed. Temporary resources were cleaned up afterward; the real fix lives only in `/workspace/app/main.go` and the rebuilt `/workspace/orders-api`.
